The assassination of William McKinley. Anarchist Leon Czolgosz shot President McKinley during a public reception in Buffalo on September sixth, nineteen oh-one, and he died eight days later from complications. Czolgosz was captured and executed within months as the nation panicked about anarchist violence. Vice President Theodore Roosevelt, at forty-two, became the youngest president in history, transforming American foreign and domestic policy. The event sparked legislation restricting anarchists from entering or residing in the United States.
